entries.title: Overview
entries.content:
Treasurer reports $15,291.07 in club funds after fees and tournament expenses.
Upcoming SCBA team play starts in January; roster deadline: December 1st.
Membership at 260 active members; slowest growth month, but renewals strong.
No new candidates for board positions; current board remains unchanged.
Christmas tournament sign-ups open Tuesday; new format and trophy case planned.
50/50 winner Tom Komp
25$ Gift Card Raffle winner: Mark Hillyer

entries.title: Treasurer's Financial Report
entries.content: Net funds available to club: $15,291.07 after fees and tournament expenses.

entries.title: SCBA Team Play & Tournament Details
entries.content:
SCGA team play starts January; matches on Jan 10, 18, 24, 31, Feb 7, 14 at 8:00 PM.
Need 12 players per match; aim for 24–30 on roster; commitment required for 6 weeks.
Format: two-man vestibule; points—2 front, 2 back, 2 overall; passes worth 1 point.
Low handicaps tee off first; tee times mostly 8:00 or 9:00.
Roster deadline: December 1st; priority to board/members present; email for interest.
Section winners advance to play other winners in California.

entries.title: Membership Status & Outreach Initiatives
entries.content:
Added 2 new members this month, slowest growth so far.
Total active members: 260.
Membership renewals increased during this period.
Membership drive scheduled for January.
Referral incentive: sign up 5 members in a year to cover own membership.

entries.title: Board Elections & Officer Roles
entries.content:
No nominations received for any board positions.
All current board members remain in their roles.
New membership director position introduced; no volunteers.

entries.content:

entries.title: Overview
entries.content:
Major tournament format changes require president or vice president approval moving forward.
Discussion of tournament participation numbers: 72-73 players in recent events.
Frustration over lack of communication and unclear rules for tournaments.
Comparison with other clubs (e.g., El Dorado) regarding club size, participation, and payouts.
Debate over club expenses (Golf Genius, Squarespace) and potential cost-saving measures.
Proposals for future tournament formats, payouts, and inclusivity (e.g., age, handicap, tee selection).

entries.title: Tournament Format Changes and Executive Oversight
entries.content:
Policy or format changes require president or vice president approval.
Tournament format changed without leadership input.
Previous tournament had 72 sign-ups; current had 73.
Change resulted in only 1 more participant.
Request for no major tournament changes without leadership sign-off.

entries.title: Communication Issues and Rule Clarity
entries.content:
Lack of clear tournament format and rules caused confusion.
Participants requested advance information on tee options and rules.
Ongoing complaints about unfinished single match play and event delays.
Proposal: Review all tournament rules and formats in January meeting.
Plan to post all tournament details, including minor events, on website.

entries.title: Club Comparisons, Participation, and Financial Concerns
entries.content:
Tournament scheduling discussed; conflicts with club events on Saturdays and Sundays.
Team play format uses random pairings by handicap, not player choice; six consecutive weeks starting January 3rd.
Roster size set at 16-32 players; priority given to those committing to all weeks.
Pace of play policy: 15-minute window, penalty stroke for violations; use of Bob Genius software debated due to $2,600-$3,000 annual cost.
Club size: 263 members vs. El Dorado's 500; survey distributed to gather feedback on participation and scheduling.

entries.title: Future Proposals: Formats, Payouts, Inclusivity
entries.content:
Planned to purchase trophies and plaques for club championship winners; Mayor's Cup trophy to be more elaborate.
Mayor's Cup scheduled for April with reduced field size (proposed top 16 qualify for match play, payout to top 16).
Discussion on tournament formats: 7 individual, 5 team tournaments; two-man tournaments in September and Turkey Shootout.
Proposed changes to skins: allow use of handicaps, consider splitting skins by tee or handicap group.
Debate on tee assignments for older/high-handicap players; suggestion to allow flexibility (e.g., play from whites or reds for seniors).

entries.content:
NO QUALIFIER THIS MONTH DUE TO LOWEST TURNOUT.
EVENT IS TWO-MAN BEST BALL, SINGLE-DAY, FLIGHTED; PAYOUTS AS USUAL.
NO HERITAGE CUP THIS YEAR.
CUPS ALTERNATE ANNUALLY: MAYOR'S CUP (INDIVIDUAL MATCH PLAY) ONE YEAR; HERITAGE CUP (TWO-MAN BEST BALL MATCH PLAY) NEXT.

entries.title: Handicap Averaging, Flighting, and Tee Assignments
entries.content:
EMAIL SET ALL PLAYERS ON BLUE TEES; PLAN: LOWER FLIGHTS/HIGH HANDICAPS ON WHITE TEES; A/B FLIGHTS ON BLUE TEES.
GOLF GENIUS AVERAGES TEAMMATES' HANDICAPS TO ASSIGN FLIGHTS.
EXAMPLE: TWO 20S → AVERAGE 20 → LOWER FLIGHT → WHITE TEES; DEPENDS ON FIELD DISTRIBUTION.
MIXED PAIR (2 + 30) COULD LAND IN LOWER FLIGHT → WHITE TEES; KEEP PARTNERS ON SAME TEES TO AVOID INEQUITY.
OPEN ITEM: CONFIRM HANDICAP-AVERAGING/TEE LOGIC IN GOLF GENIUS; METHOD FOR COMBINING HANDICAPS QUESTIONED.

entries.title: Finances, Participation, Membership, and Social Metrics
entries.content:
NET CLUB FUNDS: $13,913; Q3 GOLF GENIUS BILL PAID 2 DAYS AGO.
GOLF GENIUS COST DISCUSSED ≈$4,000; FUNDED VIA TOURNAMENT FEES AND 50-50 RAFFLE, NOT MEMBERSHIPS.
TOURNAMENT THIS SATURDAY: 72 REGISTERED; SKINS GAME THE FOLLOWING WEEK: 6 REGISTERED (5 VIA WEBSITE + 1 BOARD MEMBER).
GOLF GENIUS PROVIDES MOBILE SCORING, REAL-TIME LEADERBOARDS, AUTOMATIC SKINS/WINNINGS CALCULATION, AND MASS EMAILS/TEXTS; SAVES ADMINISTRATIVE TIME; ENABLES IMMEDIATE SCORE POSTING.
ACTIVE MEMBERS: 256; +6 SINCE LAST MEETING. SOCIAL MEDIA GROWTH SINCE TAKEOVER: +25 FOLLOWERS AND ≈2,000 VIEWS.

entries.title: Christmas Shamble: Blind Draw vs Friend Pairing
entries.content:
CHRISTMAS SHAMBLE (FOUR-MAN) PLANNED; TEAMS TARGET A/B/C/D HANDICAP MIX.
DEBATE PERSISTS: BLIND DRAW TO MIX MEMBERS VS. PAIRING WITH FRIENDS.
PAIRING PARTY TRADITION (~15 YEARS): DRAW ONE FROM A/B/C/D BUCKETS TO FORM TEAMS.
LAST YEAR: LOW ATTENDANCE; ORDERED ~20 PIZZA BOXES DESPITE FEW PARTICIPANTS; FORMAT CITED AS FACTOR.
PROPOSED COMPROMISE: DEADLINE SIGN-UP, PUBLISH FLIGHTS, ALLOW PARTIAL SELF-PAIRING, BLIND-DRAW REMAINDER; MANAGE VIA GOLF GENIUS; ADJUST HANDICAPS FOR HOMOGENEOUS TEAMS.

entries.title: Survey Plan and Away-Tournament Distance/Price Strategy
entries.content:
CLUB SURVEY SCHEDULED FOR NEXT MONTH; EMAIL WILL FOLLOW; RESULTS INFORM NEXT YEAR'S ADJUSTMENTS.
SURVEY TOPICS: SATISFACTION THIS YEAR; TEAM VS INDIVIDUAL FORMATS; MATCH PLAY FEEDBACK; ACCEPTABLE TRAVEL DISTANCE; BUDGET AND BUS OPTION.
AWAY TOURNAMENT PRICING INCREASED DUE TO RESERVED GROUP SLOTS; COSTS EXCEEDED ONLINE RATES; FUTURE NOTICES WILL CLARIFY.
PARTICIPATION/DISTANCE: MANY PREFER ≤30 MINUTES (LONG BEACH, RIO HONDO, LOS AMIGOS); OTHERS ACCEPT UP TO 50 MILES; 1 HOUR OFTEN TOO FAR; PALM SPRINGS TWO-DAY LIKELY DRAWS ~20%.

entries.title: Match Play Format, Rules, and Payouts Discussion
entries.content:
Previous match play lacked deadlines, causing delays.
No set timeframe led to elongated matches due to injuries and scheduling issues.
Proposal to set deadlines for future matches to ensure timely completion.
If a team fails to play by the deadline, top seed advances automatically.
Fewer teams expected, resulting in fewer rounds.

entries.title: Tournament Format Feedback and Adjustments for Handicaps
entries.content:
Received more positive than negative feedback on all tournament formats in 2024.
No tournament had a majority of negative feedback from participants.
Plans to adjust formats to accommodate higher handicaps, allowing play from white tees.
Specific tournament at Shambo received significant positive feedback due to unique course and strategic play.

entries.title: Communication, Email Reminders, and Member Onboarding
entries.content:

All new members receive a welcome email with website info, regardless of signup method.
Plan to increase email reminders for meetings to improve communication.
Goal to steer more members to use the website for information.
